title: Affordance mapping — inference sketchbook
notes:
Stream-of-consciousness + light structure for a feature I'd like to prototype: an 'affordance mapping' layer that helps developers signal and the platform respond with different inference affordances (fidelity/cost/response-shape) dynamically. Rough brain dump for product discussion and an A/B experiment plan.

Why I care (motivation):
- Customers want predictable cost/latency but different parts of an app have different quality needs (search vs. reply vs. assistant).
- Current approach: explicit model selection and manual batching/quantization config. Too heavyweight for product engineers.
- Idea: let app devs express intent ("high-precision", "fast-glance", "structured-extract"), and runtime maps to model variant + config + cache policy.

Problem statement (short):
- Reduce friction for choosing the right inference configuration per request without exposing low-level knobs.
- Improve unit economics by routing cheap requests to lower-cost paths and reserving expensive fast paths for high-value requests.

Goals (MVP):
- API-level affordance hints: small set of enums + freeform tags.
- Runtime policy that maps hints -> model variant, batch window, quantization profile, cache TTL.
- Telemetry: token cost, latency, per-affordance accuracy proxy (e.g., eval set pass rate).
- Opt-in A/B toggle for customers to try affordance-mapping vs. manual model pinning.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Full RL-based per-request optimization (future).
- Replacing all existing model selection controls — MVP supplements them.

Target personas / users:
- Product engineers (PLG users) who want easier tradeoffs.
- Platform engineers who want predictable capacity and smoother SLOs.
- Solutions engineers who will help enterprise customers configure policies.

Affordance taxonomy (initial proposals):
- fidelity: {low, medium, high}  // general quality/creativity tradeoffs
- speed: {interactive, batch, background}  // latency expectation
- structure: {freeform, json-schema, single-token}  // output shape hints
- safety-sensitivity: {low, medium, high}  // controls for extra moderation/filters
- cost-priority: {cheap, balanced, quality}  // explicit cost preference if conflict

Mapping examples (toy rules):
- fidelity=low, speed=interactive -> quantized-4bit-small-model, batch-window=10ms, cache-prefix=true
- fidelity=high, structure=json-schema -> float16-large-model, batch-window=0ms, validation-hook-on
- speed=background, cost-priority=cheap -> CPU-fallback + async callback

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want to mark low-risk notifications as fidelity=low so my bill drops without changing code paths.
- As an app owner, I want structured extracts with schema enforcement so I can safely ingest outputs into downstream services.
- As an SRE, I want telemetry aggregated by affordance so I can predict capacity needs and set alerts per class.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Customer can pass affordance hints in API calls (new header or JSON field).
- Platform stores affordance in trace/span and metrics pipeline (token cost, p95 latency) and shows in Console.
- Default mapping exists and reduces average cost for a set of test traffic by >=20% with <5% measured degradation on a curated eval set for low-fidelity routes.

Architecture notes (very rough):
- Config layer: affordance -> policy table (per-customer override + global defaults). Simple DSL (yaml) for mapping rules.
- Serving: policy evaluated at routing/proxy layer; outputs the model id + runtime flags (batch window, quant profile, cache key policy).
- Observability: tag spans / metrics with affordance.* and surface per-affordance dashboards and breakouts in Console.

Experiment plan (A/B):
- Phase 0: internal traffic (dev org) use affordance hints, gather mapping telemetry.
- Phase 1: opt-in PLG customers (beta) — measure cost delta, error/regression signals vs baseline.
- Metrics: cost per 1k requests, correctness proxy (eval tasks), latency p50/p95, error rate (unexpected outputs).
- Success threshold: cost down >=15% for hinted traffic and correctness degradation <3% on eval set.

Evaluation / quality checks:
- Need small eval suites per affordance profile (e.g., "low-fidelity summarization" eval set) to monitor regressions.
- Consider integrating with Optimize to recommend mapping changes after baseline run.

Rollout considerations:
- Default policy: safe conservative mapping so no surprise customer regressions.
- Allow customers to pin requests to explicit model id to opt-out.
- Provide a 'preview' mode in Console that simulates mapping for historical traces (what-if). TODO: designs for preview UX.

Edge cases / unanswered questions:
- How to measure "quality" for arbitrary app traffic? (need app-proxy eval harness or user-provided test sets)
- Conflicting hints (fidelity=high + cost=cheap) -> priority resolution rules? Probably explicit cost-priority overrides.
- Billing model: do we expose per-affordance pricing or keep per-token only and surface expected costs?
- Security: can affordance hints be abused to bypass moderation? Need mapping to safety-sensitivity and mandatory checks.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Draft minimal API spec (field name, allowed values, header vs body). (owner: Rhea)
- [ ] Prototype mapping table and simple router change in the dev env. (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Build small eval datasets for 3 affordance profiles. (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Design Console preview + per-affordance telemetry widgets. (owner: Design)
- [ ] Write a quick internal note for early beta customers (owner: Solutions eng).

Notes to self / brain dump bits:
- Could piggyback on existing session-metadata header; avoid adding too many new top-level fields.
- Might be nice to support boolean hints too (e.g., prefer_cached=true) for simple cases.
- Think about policy learning later: frequency-based routing optims, e.g., send 10% of low-fidelity to high-fidelity for drift detection. (explore canary sampling)
- Keep mapping table human-readable so SEs can tweak per-customer. YAML + priority order should suffice.

Related tickets and PRs (for context): INF-4123 (affordance API proto), PR #624 (router mapping prototype), wiki: affordance-mapping-proposal.

Meeting notes (quick):
- 2025-01-15 sync with Evan + Maya: everyone liked taxonomy, concern about evaluation effort. Action: Maya to draft eval templates by 1/24.
- 2025-01-28 infra check: SRE ok with adding one span tag per request; asked for sampling fallback to avoid metric explosion.

Final thought (for now):
- This seems like a good middleground between full auto-optimization and manual control. If we can get a pleasant UX and clear initial defaults, adoption could be high among PLG users who don't want to tune LLMs continuously.

-- RK
